correctness.rationale: The normalized payoff is algebraically exactly r(13/30−x/60+x²/30)−1; roots are real and ordered in 30/13<r<160/69. The Fermi transition probabilities form a valid absorbing nearest-neighbor chain, with ratio exp(−wF). The exact harmonic fixation sum and exact discrete quadratic potential are reconstructed. Uniform polynomial Euler–Maclaurin and boundary geometric-series arguments supply the boundary mass; a nondegenerate lattice Laplace argument at the unique interior potential minimum supplies its Gaussian mass and exact Euler–Maclaurin half-endpoint factor. Comparing the masses gives the full prefactor trichotomy, and their uniform parameter-dependent versions give the moving logarithmic crossover. The derivative \(D'(1920/829)=829/5120\) and three rational witnesses were independently checked algebraically; log-domain exact-lattice numerical tests of all regimes and moving crossover passed. Finite tests are supplementary and not an infinite proof. The claim explicitly excludes degenerate roots, changing selection strength, and identity with the original finite hypergraph process.

originality.rationale: The finite-population expected-payoff Fermi closure and its exact three-regime, prefactor-resolved large-population fixation asymptotics and logarithmic finite-size crossover for the specified mixed two/three-player nonlinear game are not supplied by the examined papers. The foundation—Fermi update and exact birth–death fixation sum—is explicitly prior; the source already gives both deterministic interior equilibria. The model-specific potential competition, counterintuitive zero critical fixation, and shifted crossover require an additional two-site lattice asymptotic analysis. Full certainty against all unindexed general results is not claimed.
residual_risks: An unindexed general theorem for arbitrary analytic one-dimensional Fermi payoff fields with boundary and interior competing minimizers may immediately imply the asymptotic form, although no specific stronger source was identified.
The PNAS multiplayer comparison was available through indexed article text but a direct PMC full-text view met an access challenge.
The expected-payoff closure must not be conflated with the motivating microscopic finite-hypergraph process.

value.rationale: The motivating work establishes coexistence–cooperation bistability and reports stochastic quasistationary branches, but equilibrium phase diagrams cannot predict which absorbing outcome ultimately wins in finite populations. Within one natural fixed-payoff Fermi closure, the benefit parameter induces a sharp change from exponentially suppressed full-cooperation fixation to almost-sure fixation, with the critical point itself having a counterintuitive vanishing \(N^{-1/2}\) probability and a nontrivial logistic transition only after a \((\log N)/N\) displacement. This is an exact, independently motivated stochastic-selection classification rather than a relabelled equilibrium or a bare numerical table. Attribution distinguishes standard Fermi fixation identities and Laplace methods from the new specific quantitative conclusion.
